{{2024–25 Southeastern Conference men's basketball standings}}
The '''2024–25 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Kentucky]] during the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Wildcats, founding members of the [[Southeastern Conference]], played their home games at [[Rupp Arena]] and were led by [[Mark Pope]] in his first season as head coach for the Wildcats.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lewis |first1=Will |title=Printable 2024-25 UK Basketball Schedule; TV Broadcasts and More - Sports Brackets |url=https://sportsbrackets.net/2024/07/01/printable-2024-25-uk-basketball-schedule-tv-broadcasts-and-more/ |website=Sports Brackets |publisher=NCAAB |access-date=11 October 2024 |date=2 July 2024}}</ref>

The Kentucky Wildcats drew an average home attendance of 20,334, the 2nd-highest of all basketball teams in the world.<ref>https://www.espn.com/nba/attendance/_/year/2025/sort/homeTotal</ref><ref>https://stats.ncaa.org/rankings/change_sport_year_div</ref>

==Previous season==
The [[2023–24 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Wildcats]] finished the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]] with a record of 23–8, 13–5 in SEC play to finish in a 3-way tie for second place in the SEC. Despite being the number two seed in the [[2024 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]], they were upset in the quarterfinal round by [[2023–24 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they got upset by [[2023–24 Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball team|Oakland]] in the first round, finishing the season with an overall record of 23–10 record.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Clay |first1=John |title=Three takeaways from Kentucky basketball's loss to Oakland in the NCAA Tournament |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/spt-columns-blogs/sidelines-with-john-clay/article286956040.html |website=kentucky.com |publisher=Lexington Herald-Leader |access-date=November 13, 2024 |date=March 31, 2024}}</ref> This marked [[John Calipari]]'s final season as Kentucky's head coach, he left for Arkansas a month later.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=John Calipari officially hired as Arkansas men's basketball coach |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/39913931/john-calipari-officially-hired-arkansas-men-basketball-coach |website=espn.com |publisher=ESPN |access-date=November 13, 2024 |date=April 10, 2024}}</ref>
